title: Sell Mineral Rights in Reader, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Reader, WV
metaDescription: Reader, Wetzel County mineral owners: core Marcellus farmland near New Martinsville, multi-lease history, and family heir fractional interests.
heroLead: Reader is a small Wetzel County community close to New Martinsville, sitting in ground that's been part of the county's sustained core Marcellus development.
intro: Given Wetzel County's standing as some of the thickest Marcellus acreage in the state, Reader's surrounding farmland has seen consistent leasing interest over the past decade and a half, layered onto family tracts that have often been held locally for generations.

sections.heading: Consistent leasing activity near New Martinsville
paragraphs: Reader's proximity to New Martinsville, the county seat and a hub of drilling activity, means tracts here have generally seen earlier and more consistent leasing interest than more remote parts of the county. That also means more opportunity for a tract's governing lease to have changed hands through assignment over the years.

sections.heading: Family tracts and heir shares
paragraphs: Ownership around Reader typically follows the county's broader pattern — farm tracts split among multiple heirs after several generations, each holding a sellable fractional share of the underlying mineral estate. Confirming your exact percentage takes a courthouse records check rather than relying on an old division order alone.

sections.heading: Checking whether your Reader lease includes a Pugh clause
paragraphs: Some Wetzel County leases, particularly more recent ones, include a Pugh clause limiting how much of your acreage an operator can hold under a single well versus what reverts to you if undeveloped. Whether your Reader-area lease has this provision affects what happens to any portion of your tract outside an active unit.
Reviewing the actual lease language — not only the division order — is the only way to confirm whether this applies to your interest.

faqs.question: Has my Reader-area lease likely changed operators?
faqs.answer: It's common in this part of Wetzel County given the volume of leasing activity. Confirming the current operator of record and reviewing your division orders is worthwhile.

faqs.question: How many heirs typically hold a Reader-area family tract?
faqs.answer: Multiple heirs sharing one original interest is common after several generations of local family ownership.

faqs.question: Where would I check the current lease status for my Reader tract?
faqs.answer: The Wetzel County Courthouse in New Martinsville holds the deed and lease records needed to confirm current status.

faqs.question: What does a Pugh clause do if my Reader lease has one?
faqs.answer: It typically releases the portion of your acreage outside an actively producing unit, rather than holding your entire tract under one small producing well indefinitely.

faqs.question: How do I request my unit plat if I don't know who operates my Reader-area well?
faqs.answer: A courthouse records check will identify the operator of record and any filed pooling documents, which you can then request directly or have pulled as part of a title review.
